digest.component_or_area: DC outbound comment and description length convergence testing
propositions: DC lacks convergence test suites for oversized comments and descriptions that Cloud possesses, creating risk that truncation diverges across passes and re-emits mutations indefinitely

The DC comment and description sanitizer both bind to WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767), the documented default of jira.text.field.character.limit which governs Comments and Text custom fields equally by design, per jpm.xml and JRASERVER-28519

Existing convergence test injection points (_diff_comments sanitizer= parameter, compute_outbound_mutations backend parameters) accept explicit DC backend instances but tests risk silently falling back to Cloud's backend via select_backend(load_config()) if any required argument is omitted

DC and Cloud truncate comments identically (same 32767 limit and marker suffix) so comment convergence proof cannot rest on value assertions alone and must verify the injected DC sanitizer actually executed via identity or recording checks
DC truncates descriptions at 32767 plain characters while Cloud truncates at 32000 ADF-serialized characters, providing a genuine value-based discriminator to prove DC's path executed

The max_chars binding in backend.py:146-149 lacks provenance documentation citing jira.text.field.character.limit, allowing readers to misinterpret 32767 as an assumption rather than the documented instance default
